readings.title: How Can Man Be Right with God?
readings.subtitle: Job acknowledges the immense and unchallengeable power of Elohim.
readings.text: [Job 9:1] And Iyoḇ answered and said, [2] “Truly <dn>I</dn> know it is so. But how is man right with <dn>Elohim</dn>? [3] If one wished to dispute with <dn>Him</dn>, he would not answer <dn>Him</dn> one time out of a thousand. [4] Wise in heart and potent of power – who has hardened himself against <dn>Him</dn> and is at peace? [5] <dn>He</dn> who removes mountains, and they do not know it, when <dn>He</dn> overturns them in <dn>His</dn> displeasure; [6] who shakes <dn>את</dn> the earth out of its place, and its columns tremble; [7] who commands the sun, and it does not rise; and <dn>He</dn> seals up <dn>את</dn> the stars, [8] stretching out <dn>את</dn> the heavens by <dn>Himself</dn>, and treading upon the waves of the sea; [9] who made Ash, Kesil, and Kimah, and <dn>את</dn> the rooms of the south; [10] who performs great and unsearchable deeds, and innumerable wonders. [11] Look, <dn>He</dn> goes by me, and <dn>I</dn> do not see; and <dn>He</dn> moves past, but <dn>I</dn> do not discern <dn>Him</dn>. [12] Look, <dn>He</dn> snatches away, who brings it back? Who says to <dn>Him</dn>, ‘What are <dn>You</dn> doing?’ [13] <dn>Eloah</dn> does not turn back <dn>His</dn> displeasure, the helpers of pride stoop under <dn>Him</dn>.

readings.title: The Futility of Arguing with the Almighty
readings.subtitle: Job laments that God destroys both the innocent and the guilty.
readings.text: [Job 9:14] How much less would <dn>I</dn> answer <dn>Him</dn>, choose <dn>my</dn> words with <dn>Him</dn>? [15] For though <dn>I</dn> were righteous, <dn>I</dn> would not answer <dn>Him</dn>. <dn>I</dn> pray to <dn>Him</dn> for <dn>my</dn> right-ruling. [16] Though <dn>I</dn> had called and <dn>He</dn> answered me, <dn>I</dn> would not believe that <dn>He</dn> was listening to <dn>my</dn> voice. [17] For <dn>He</dn> crushes me with a storm, and has multiplied <dn>my</dn> wounds for no cause. [18] <dn>He</dn> does not allow me to recover <dn>my</dn> breath, but fills me with bitterness. [19] If <dn>I</dn> speak of power? Look, <dn>He</dn> is potent. And if of right-ruling? Who sets me a time? [20] If <dn>I</dn> am righteous? <dn>My</dn> mouth would declare me wrong. Am <dn>I</dn> perfect? It would declare me perverse. [21] Am <dn>I</dn> perfect? Do <dn>I</dn> not know <dn>my</dn> own being? <dn>I</dn> despise <dn>my</dn> life! [22] It is all the same, therefore <dn>I</dn> say, ‘<dn>He</dn> destroys the perfect and the wrong.’ [23] If the scourge slays suddenly, <dn>He</dn> laughs at the trial of the innocent. [24] Earth has been given into the hand of the wrong. <dn>He</dn> covers <dn>את</dn> the faces of its judges. If it is not <dn>He</dn>, then who is it?

readings.title: Longing for a Mediator
readings.subtitle: Job's days fly by as he despairs of finding justice.
readings.text: [Job 9:25] <dn>My</dn> days have become swifter than a runner – they have fled, they have not seen good. [26] They have passed by like swift ships, like an eagle swooping on its prey. [27] If <dn>I</dn> say, ‘Let me forget <dn>my</dn> complaint, let me put off <dn>my</dn> sad face, and let me smile,’ [28] <dn>I</dn> shall be afraid of all <dn>my</dn> sufferings. <dn>I</dn> know that <dn>You</dn> do not hold me innocent. [29] If <dn>I</dn> am wrong, why should <dn>I</dn> labour in vain? [30] If <dn>I</dn> washed <dn>myself</dn> with snow water, and cleansed <dn>my</dn> hands with soap, [31] then <dn>You</dn> would plunge me into a ditch, and <dn>my</dn> garments shall abhor me. [32] For <dn>He</dn> is not a man as <dn>I</dn> am that <dn>I</dn> answer <dn>Him</dn>, and we come together into right-ruling. [33] There is no mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both. [34] Let <dn>Him</dn> take <dn>His</dn> rod away from me, and let not <dn>His</dn> dread frighten me. [35] Then <dn>I</dn> would speak and not fear <dn>Him</dn>, for <dn>I</dn> am not so within <dn>myself</dn>.

readings.title: Job's Complaint to His Creator
readings.subtitle: Why did You form me only to destroy me?
readings.text: [Job 10:1] “<dn>My</dn> being has grown weary of life. <dn>I</dn> let loose <dn>my</dn> complaint, <dn>I</dn> speak in the bitterness of <dn>my</dn> being. [2] <dn>I</dn> say to <dn>Eloah</dn>, ‘Do not declare me wrong, show me why <dn>You</dn> strive with me. [3] Is it good to <dn>You</dn> that <dn>You</dn> should crush, that <dn>You</dn> should despise the work of <dn>Your</dn> hands, and shine on the counsel of the wrong? [4] Do <dn>You</dn> have eyes of flesh? Do <dn>You</dn> see as man sees? [5] Are <dn>Your</dn> days like the days of a mortal man? Are <dn>Your</dn> years like the days of a mighty man, [6] that <dn>You</dn> should seek for <dn>my</dn> crookedness and search out <dn>my</dn> sin? [7] For <dn>You</dn> know that <dn>I</dn> am not wrong, and there is no one to deliver from <dn>Your</dn> hand. [8] <dn>Your</dn> hands have made me and shaped me, together all around, yet <dn>You</dn> destroy me. [9] Remember, please, that <dn>You</dn> have made me like clay. And would <dn>You</dn> turn me into dust again? [10] Did <dn>You</dn> not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese? [11] Skin and flesh <dn>You</dn> put on me, and wove me with <dn>את</dn> bones and sinews. [12] Life and loving-commitment <dn>You</dn> have bestowed on me, and <dn>Your</dn> visitation has preserved <dn>my</dn> spirit.

readings.title: A Plea for Respite Before Death
readings.subtitle: Job wishes for death and describes the land of darkness.
readings.text: [Job 10:13] And these <dn>You</dn> have laid up in <dn>Your</dn> heart, <dn>I</dn> know that this was with <dn>You</dn>: [14] If <dn>I</dn> sin, then <dn>You</dn> watch me, and let no crookedness of mine go unpunished. [15] If <dn>I</dn> am wrong, woe to me! And if <dn>I</dn> am righteous, <dn>I</dn> would not lift up <dn>my</dn> head – filled with shame and seeing <dn>my</dn> grief! [16] If <dn>I</dn> lift it up high, <dn>You</dn> hunt me as a lion, and again <dn>You</dn> would show <dn>Yourself</dn> marvellous against me. [17] <dn>You</dn> renew <dn>Your</dn> witnesses against me, and increase <dn>Your</dn> vexation toward me; changes and a host are with me. [18] So why have <dn>You</dn> brought me forth from the womb? Oh, that <dn>I</dn> had perished and no eye had seen me! [19] <dn>I</dn> should have been as though <dn>I</dn> had not been – brought from the womb to the burial-site. [20] Are not <dn>my</dn> days few? Then cease! Leave me alone, so that <dn>I</dn> brighten up a little, [21] Before <dn>I</dn> go, and not return, to the land of darkness and the shadow of death, [22] a land as dark as darkness itself, as the shadow of death, without any order, whose light is as darkness.”

readings.title: Zophar Rebukes Job
readings.subtitle: He accuses Job of empty talk and claims God's wisdom is unsearchable.
readings.text: [Job 11:1] And Tsophar the Na‛amathite answered and said, [2] “Should a multitude of words go unanswered? And should a man of lips be declared right? [3] Should your babblings silence men? And should you mock, and no one make you ashamed? [4] Since you have said, ‘<dn>My</dn> discourse is flawless, and <dn>I</dn> have been clean in <dn>Your</dn> eyes.’ [5] But if only <dn>Eloah</dn> would speak, and open <dn>His</dn> lips against you, [6] and show you <dn>את</dn> the secrets of wisdom, doubling your ability. Know then that <dn>Eloah</dn> forgets some of your crookedness for you. [7] Would you find out <dn>Eloah</dn> by searching, or search out the end of the Almighty? [8] It is higher than the heavens – what would you do? Deeper than She’ol – what would you know? [9] Their measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea. [10] If <dn>He</dn> passes through and shuts up, and gathers, then who does reverse it? [11] For <dn>He</dn> knows false men. When <dn>He</dn> sees wickedness does <dn>He</dn> not consider it? [12] But a senseless man takes heart when a wild donkey’s colt is born a man!

readings.title: A Call to Repentance
readings.subtitle: Zophar promises restoration if Job puts away his iniquity.
readings.text: [Job 11:13] If you would prepare your heart, and stretch out your hands toward <dn>Him</dn>; [14] if wickedness were in your hand, put it far away and do not let <dn>את</dn> perverseness dwell in your tents; [15] then indeed you shall lift up your face without spot; and you shall stand firm, and not be afraid, [16] because you would forget sorrow, and remember it as waters that have passed away, [17] and your life would be brighter than noon. You would soar upward, you would be like the morning. [18] And you shall trust, because there is expectancy. And when you have searched you shall lie down in safety. [19] And you shall rest, and no one would make you afraid, and many shall seek your favour. [20] But the eyes of the wrong are consumed, and they shall not escape, and their expectancy is the breathing out of life!”

readings.title: Wisdom Is Not Yours Alone
readings.subtitle: Job sarcastically responds to his friends and points to creation's testimony.
readings.text: [Job 12:1] And Iyoḇ answered and said, [2] “Truly you are the people, and wisdom would die with you! [3] But <dn>I</dn>, like you, have a heart too; <dn>I</dn> am not less than you. And who does not know such as these? [4] <dn>I</dn> have become a laughing-stock to <dn>my</dn> friends – one who has called on <dn>Eloah</dn> and <dn>He</dn> answered him! A laughing-stock is the righteous, the perfect one! [5] A lamp is despised in the thought of one who is at ease – prepared for those whose feet slip. [6] The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke <dn>Ěl</dn> are complacent, to him who brings <dn>Eloah</dn> into his hand! [7] But now ask the beasts, and they teach you; and the birds of the heavens, and they declare it to you; [8] or speak to the earth, and it teaches you; and the fish of the sea inform you. [9] Who among all these does not know that the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done <dn>את</dn> this, [10] in whose hand is <dn>את</dn> the life of all that live, and <dn>את</dn> the breath of all mankind? [11] Does the ear not try <dn>את</dn> words? And the mouth taste food for itself? [12] With the aged is wisdom, and understanding with length of days.

readings.title: God's Absolute Sovereignty
readings.subtitle: He brings down rulers and makes judges go mad.
readings.text: [Job 12:13] With <dn>Him</dn> are wisdom and might, <dn>He</dn> has counsel and understanding. [14] Look, <dn>He</dn> breaks down, and it is not rebuilt. If <dn>He</dn> imprisons a man, there is no release. [15] Look, <dn>He</dn> withholds the waters, and they dry up. And <dn>He</dn> sends them out, and they overwhelm the earth. [16] With <dn>Him</dn> are strength and ability. The misled and the misleader are <dn>His</dn>. [17] <dn>He</dn> leads counsellors away stripped, and makes judges go mad. [18] <dn>He</dn> loosens the bonds of sovereigns, and binds a girdle on their loins; [19] who leads away <dn>את</dn> priests as a spoil, and overthrows the mighty; [20] turning aside the lip of the trusted ones, and takes away <dn>את</dn> the discernment of the elders; [21] pouring scorn on nobles, and loosens <dn>את</dn> the girdle of the strong; [22] revealing <dn>את</dn> deep matters out of darkness, and <dn>He</dn> brings the shadow of death to light; [23] making nations great, and <dn>He</dn> destroys them; spreading out the nations, and <dn>He</dn> leads them out. [24] turning aside <dn>את</dn> the heart of the chiefs of the people of the earth, and <dn>He</dn> makes them wander in a pathless waste. [25] They grope in darkness, having no light, and <dn>He</dn> makes them stagger like a drunkard.
